sketches.title: Hall Pass Chain
sketches.premise: You are students trying to cross a school corridor while every player adds one obstacle that defeats the last obstacle. The corridor gets nastier until someone proposes a move that cannot plausibly stop what stands.
sketches.criterion: A move overcomes the standing obstacle by directly blocking, removing, exposing, or neutralizing its effect; merely going around it, enduring it, making a larger copy, or claiming it is harmless loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one standing school-corridor obstacle and state its direct counter: "I am a janitor's mop bucket, spilling across the floor to stop the charging bully."

sketches.title: Bell to Bell
sketches.premise: The corridor is trapped between bells, and each turn introduces one standing school force that defeats the previous force. Your chain must make the next bell more inevitable; one weak link and the hallway keeps you.
sketches.criterion: The new force must directly stop, cancel, or control what the previous force does; fleeing it, waiting it out, surviving it, or offering a stronger version of the same force does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Name a force and its action in one sentence: "I am a fire drill, emptying the corridor and silencing the stampede."

sketches.title: Locker Room Temperature
sketches.premise: Every turn changes the corridor's standing mood, rumor, or social pressure, and the next player must defeat that pressure with a new school-hall reality. The host records each failed mood swing like a failed experiment in human misery.
sketches.criterion: A move wins only if its social or physical reality directly breaks, reveals, redirects, or neutralizes the pressure before it; ignoring it, enduring it, or intensifying the same pressure loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name a standing corridor condition and what defeats it: "I am a teacher's clipboard, turning the whispered cheating rumor into names and consequences."
sketches.first_card: A whisper that everyone heard the test is cancelled.

sketches.title: Stairwell Supply
sketches.premise: The corridor is a survival route stocked with ordinary school objects, and each player places one object that defeats the previous object by what it can plainly do. No magic excuses: the nastiest triumphs come from lockers, tape, water, scissors, books, and gravity.
sketches.criterion: The chosen object must use a clear everyday function to block, bind, cut, soak, trap, expose, or otherwise disable the standing object; dodging it, being too small to matter, or using a bigger duplicate loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one object, its physical action, and its target: "I am duct tape, sealing the marker's cap shut before it can write on the wall."
sketches.first_card: A permanent marker uncapped over the principal's sign.

sketches.title: Office Referral
sketches.premise: The corridor has become a chain of school discipline: each turn states one standing excuse, accusation, or rule breach, then defeats it with a new piece of evidence or authority. The judge is the assistant principal's clipboard, and it has no sympathy for decorative bullshit.
sketches.criterion: A move overcomes the standing claim by directly disproving it, making it impossible, or placing it under a stronger plainly relevant rule; changing the subject, denying without support, or escalating the same claim loses.
sketches.move_shape: State a school claim and the evidence that defeats it: "I am a timestamped hallway camera, disproving 'I was never here.'"

sketches.title: Corridor Court
sketches.premise: Two hallway lawyers argue through concrete school objects and events: each move is a standing exhibit that defeats the previous exhibit. The host delivers the verdict with the warmth of a detention slip and the precision of a paper cut.
sketches.criterion: The new exhibit must directly invalidate, contain, reveal, or override the prior exhibit's practical meaning; surviving its implication, sidestepping it, using a cousin from the same family, or merely making the claim louder loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name an exhibit and explain its mechanism: "I am the wet-floor sign, proving the mysterious puddle is fresh and making the 'nothing happened' story collapse."
sketches.first_card: A torn note reading: "Meet me after last bell."
